evals.prompt: This repo has a review report listing 12 findings across src/auth.py (3 critical), src/query.py (2 high), and src/views.py (7 low), each with a file:line reference and a described failure. Run render review on it.
assertions: an HTML file is written under .cc-arsenal/renders/ with a name starting 'review-'
all 12 findings appear on the page, none invented and none dropped
the severity ranking from the source report is preserved, critical before high before low
each finding is inside an element carrying a data-anchor derived from its file, line and a slug of its claim, so two findings on the same line do not collide, and never from its position in the list
each finding carries fix / won't fix / discuss verdict controls
the page contains a <script id="state" type="application/json"> block holding the verdict and comment state

the page's CSS defines its palette as custom properties on a bare :root selector, redefines them under a prefers-color-scheme dark media query guarded against [data-theme="light"], and redefines them again under :root[data-theme="dark"]
body has an explicit background drawn from a token, not left transparent
the response reports the output path and the finding counts, and does not claim to have fixed anything
the publish call supplies a favicon, which the Artifact contract requires on a first publish

evals.prompt: Run render plan on a 5-step implementation plan for adding rate limiting, where steps 3 and 4 both depend on step 2.
assertions: every anchored block carries both data-anchor and data-label attributes
each anchored block contains a comment affordance control that is reachable without a mouse, revealed on :focus-within or :focus-visible and not on :hover alone
on viewports under roughly 760px the comment affordance is statically visible rather than hover-dependent
the comment composer opens inline beneath the block rather than as a modal dialog
a saved comment records anchor, label, section and text, not the anchor alone
step dependencies shown on the page come from the plan itself, and step 3 and step 4 are both shown depending on step 2
the page does not fabricate a dependency between consecutive steps that the plan did not state

evals.prompt: Run render /review-security on the current branch.
assertions: review-security is run to completion first, and the page renders the findings it actually produced
no file under skills/review-security/ is created or modified
the finding claims are carried over in the source skill's wording rather than paraphrased
the severity ranking produced by review-security is preserved on the page
file:line evidence from each finding appears on its anchored block
the response does not add findings that review-security did not report

evals.prompt: Run render docs/plans/auth-rework.md. The file is a markdown document containing an ordered list of implementation steps with a dependencies section.
assertions: the file is read before any mode is chosen
the response states which mode it selected and why, in one line, before building the page
plan mode is selected, matching the file's ordered-steps-with-dependencies shape
the plan's own step wording and ordering are preserved rather than rewritten during conversion
the original markdown file is not modified

evals.prompt: The page at .cc-arsenal/renders/prd-lachesis-2026-08-30.html was marked by the user and saved. It carries a comment anchored to req-PRD-FR-099, which no longer exists in the current requirement set. Read the marks back.
assertions: the page's state block is parsed rather than the rendered DOM being scraped
results are grouped by what the user decided rather than by page order
the comment on req-PRD-FR-099 is reported using its stored label and section and explicitly flagged as attached to something no longer present
the orphaned comment is not silently dropped from the report
the response acts on the returned marks rather than asking the user to restate them
the report covers page-level decisions, per-anchor verdicts and comments, not verdicts alone
the response lists the available modes with what each one produces
the response asks which mode the user wants
no mode is guessed and no page is built
no file is written under .cc-arsenal/renders/ or anywhere else

evals.prompt: Run render /git-commit on my staged changes.
assertions: no page is built for git-commit's output
the response explains that git-commit produces an action rather than a set of findings or decisions, so a page adds nothing
the response offers running git-commit directly instead
no commit is created as a side effect of the explanation

evals.prompt: The page at .cc-arsenal/renders/review-auth-2026-08-30.html already carries 40 verdicts and 6 comments saved by the user. Re-run render review on the same subject after two of the findings were fixed, writing to that same path.
assertions: the existing page's state block is read and parsed before the new page is written
the regenerated page embeds the carried state rather than an empty {"verdicts":{},"comments":[]} block
verdicts whose anchors no longer exist are dropped, since the findings they judged are gone
comments whose anchors no longer exist are retained in state and reported as orphaned rather than discarded
verdicts and comments on the findings that still exist are still present and still attached to them after the rebuild

evals.prompt: Run render plan on a 6-step migration plan in an environment with no Artifact tool available.
assertions: a self-contained HTML file is written and its path is reported
the response does not claim to have published anything or return an artifact link
the page's save control regenerates the document and offers it as a download rather than relying on the browser's own Save Page As
the response tells the user to replace the file at the reported path with the downloaded copy and say when done
the response does not tell the user their browser can save the marks into the original file in place
